Transport\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass RemoteExecutionRuntime:\n    \"\"\"Worker-aware execution runtime.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        pipeline_version: str = PIPELINE_VERSION,\n        runtime_spec_version: str = RUNTIME_SPEC_VERSION,\n        registry: Any = None,\n        transport: Optional[Transport] = None,\n        worker_protocol_version: str = self._registry().check_version_compatibility(\n            registration, self.pipeline_version, self.runtime_spec_version,\n        ).compatible\n\n    @staticmethod\n    def _to_request(payload: Any, affinity: ExecutionAffinity) -> WorkerRequest:\n        if isinstance(payload, WorkerRequest):\n            return payload\n        if isinstance(payload, dict):\n            text = request={\"text\": text, \"transport\": transport, **metadata},\n            pipeline_version=\"1.0\",\n            runtime_spec_version=\"1.0\",\n            worker_protocol_version=\"1.0\",\n            tenant_id=affinity.tenant_id,\n            capability=affinity.capability,\n        )\n\n    def select_worker(self, affinity: ExecutionAffinity) -> Optional[WorkerRegistration]:\n        \"\"\"Pick the first compatible, eligible worker (None if none).\"\"\"\n        registry = self._registry()\n        candidates = registry.discover(\n            tenant_id=affinity.tenant_id,   "path": "core/distribution/pool.py",
  "instructions": "Real WorkerPool with round-robin selection and unhealthy eviction.",
  "content": "\"\"\"WorkerPool — round-robin placement across eligible workers.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Iterable, Optional\n\nfrom core.distribution.contracts import WorkerStatus\nfrom core.distribution.registry import WorkerRegistration\n\n\nclass WorkerPool:\n    \"\"\"Round-robin pool over registered workers.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, workers: Optional[Iterable[WorkerRegistration]] = None) -> None:\n        self._workers: list[WorkerRegistration] = []\n        self._cursor: int = 0\n        for worker in workers or ():\n            self.add_worker(worker)\n\n    # ── membership ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    def add_worker(self, registration: WorkerRegistration) -> WorkerRegistration:\n        if not isinstance(registration, WorkerRegistration):\n            raise TypeError(\"add_worker() expects a WorkerRegistration\")\n        self.remove_worker(registration.worker_id)\n        self._workers.append(registration)\n        return registration\n\n    def remove_worker(self, worker_id: str) -> bool:\n        before = len(self._workers)\n        self._workers = [w for w in self._workers if w.worker_id != str(worker_id)]\n        return len(self._workers) != before\n\n    def workers(self) -> list:\n        return list(self._workers)\n\n    def __len__(self) -> int:\n        return len(self._workers)\n\n    # ── selection ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    def _eligible(self, tenant_id: Optional[str] = None,\n                  capability: Optional[str] = None) -> list:\n        out = []\n        for reg in self._workers:\n            if reg.status != WorkerStatus.ONLINE:\n                continue\n            if tenant_id is not None and reg.tenant_id != tenant_id:\n                continue\n            if capability and not reg.supports(capability):\n                continue\n            out.append(reg)\n        return out\n\n    def next_worker(self, tenant_id: Optional[str] = None,\n                    capability: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[WorkerRegistration]:\n        \"\"\"Round-robin over eligible workers (None when none are eligible).\"\"\"\n        eligible = self._eligible(tenant_id=tenant_id, capability=capability)\n        if not eligible:\n            return None\n        chosen = eligible[self._cursor % len(eligible)]\n        self._cursor = (self._cursor + 1) % max(1, len(self._workers))\n        return chosen\n\n    def evict_unhealthy(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Drop workers that are not ONLINE. Returns the number evicted.\"\"\"\n        unhealthy = [w for w in self._workers if w.status != WorkerStatus.ONLINE]\n        for worker in unhealthy:\n            self.remove_worker(worker.worker_id)\n        return len(unhealthy)\n\n\n__all__ = [\"WorkerPool\"]\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"HealthChecker — marks workers OFFLINE after missed heartbeats.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport asyncio\nimport logging\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\nfrom core.distribution.contracts import WorkerStatus\nfrom core.distribution.registry import get_worker_registry\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30.0\nDEFAULT_MISSED_THRESHOLD = 3\n\n\ndef _utcnow() -> datetime:\n    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)\n\n\nclass HealthChecker:\n    \"\"\"Periodically verifies workers are still heartbeating.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, interval_seconds: float = DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS,\n                 missed_heartbeat_threshold: int = DEFAULT_MISSED_THRESHOLD,\n                 registry: Any = None) -> None:\n        self.interval_seconds = float(interval_seconds)\n        self.missed_heartbeat_threshold = int(missed_heartbeat_threshold)\n        self.registry = registry\n        self._task: Optional[asyncio.Task] = None\n        self._running = False\n\n    def _registry(self) -> Any:\n        return self.registry if self.registry is not None else get_worker_registry()\n\n    @property\n    def grace_seconds(self) -> float:\n        return self.interval_seconds * max(1, self.missed_heartbeat_threshold)\n\n    # ── checks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    def is_stale(self, registration: Any, now: Optional[datetime] = None) -> bool:\n        last = getattr(registration, \"last_heartbeat\", None)\n        if last is None:\n            return True\n        if last.tzinfo is None:\n            last = last.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)\n        now = now or _utcnow()\n        return (now - last).total_seconds() > self.grace_seconds\n\n    def _check_all(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Mark every stale worker offline. Returns how many were marked.\"\"\"\n        marked = 0\n        registry = self._registry()\n        for registration in registry.all_workers():\n            if self.is_stale(registration):\n                if registration.status != WorkerStatus.OFFLINE:\n                    registration.status = WorkerStatus.OFFLINE\n                    marked += 1\n                    logger.info(\"worker %s marked offline (missed heartbeats)\",\n                                registration.worker_id)\n        return marked\n\n    def check_worker(self, worker_id: str) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Force a health check on one worker; True when it is offline.\"\"\"\n        registry = self._registry()\n        registration = registry.get(worker_id)\n        if registration is None:\n            return True\n        if self.is_stale(registration):\n            registration.status = WorkerStatus.OFFLINE\n            return True\n        return False\n\n    # ── background loop ─────────────────────────────────────────────\n    async def _run(self) -> None:\n        while self._running:\n            try:\n                self._check_all()\n            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — the loop must survive\n                logger.warning(\"health check failed: %s\", exc)\n            await asyncio.sleep(self.interval_seconds)\n\n    def start(self) -> Optional[asyncio.Task]:\n        if self._running:\n            return self._task\n        self._running = True\n        try:\n            self._task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._run())\n        except RuntimeError:  # no running loop — caller drives _check_all()\n            self._running = False\n            self._task = None\n        return self._task\n\n    async def stop(self) -> None:\n        self._running = False\n        if self._task is not None:\n            self._task.cancel()\n            try:\n                await self._task\n            except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):  # noqa: BLE001\n                pass\n            self._task = None\n\n\n__all__ = [\"HealthChecker\", \"DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS\", \"DEFAULT_MISSED_THRESHOLD\"]\n"
}

  "path": "core/distribution/retry.py",
  "instructions": "Real RetryPolicy with backoff and optional fallback.",
  "content": "\"\"\"RetryPolicy — bounded retries with optional fallback.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport asyncio\nimport inspect\nimport logging\nfrom typing import Any, Callable, Optional, Tuple\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 3\nDEFAULT_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 0.5\n\n\nclass RetryPolicy:\n    \"\"\"Runs an async callable with bounded retries and a fallback.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, max_retries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES,\n                 backoff_seconds: float = DEFAULT_BACKOFF_SECONDS,\n                 retry_on: Tuple[type, ...] = (Exception,)) -> None:\n        self.max_retries = max(1, int(max_retries))\n        self.backoff_seconds = float(backoff_seconds)\n        self.retry_on = retry_on or (Exception,)\n        self.last_error: Optional[BaseException] = None\n        self.attempts: int = 0\n\n    async def execute(self, fn: Callable, *args: Any,\n                      fallback: Optional[Callable] = None, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Call ``fn`` up to ``max_retries`` times, then ``fallback``.\n\n        Raises the last error when every attempt failed and no fallback was\n        supplied.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.attempts = 0\n        self.last_error = None\n        for attempt in range(self.max_retries):\n            self.attempts = attempt + 1\n            try:\n                result = fn(*args, **kwargs)\n                if inspect.isawaitable(result):\n                    result = await result\n                return result\n            except self.retry_on as exc:  # noqa: PERF203 — retry loop\n                self.last_error = exc\n                logger.debug(\"attempt %d/%d failed: %s\",\n                             attempt + 1, self.max_retries, exc)\n                if attempt + 1 < self.max_retries and self.backoff_seconds:\n                    await asyncio.sleep(self.backoff_seconds)\n\n        if fallback is not None:\n            result = fallback()\n            if inspect.isawaitable(result):\n                result = await result\n            return result\n        if self.last_error is not None:\n            raise self.last_error\n        raise RuntimeError(\"retry policy exhausted without an error\")  # pragma: no cover\n\n\n__all__ = [\"RetryPolicy\", \"DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES\", \"DEFAULT_BACKOFF_SECONDS\"]\n"
}

{
  "path": "core/distribution/observation.py",
  "instructions": "Observation forwarding that stamps worker_id for provenance.",
  "content": "\"\"\"Forward observations produced by remote workers.\n\nEvery forwarded observation is stamped with the originating ``worker_id``\nso traces remain attributable across the cluster (Rule 40).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport dataclasses\nimport logging\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable, Optional\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef stamp_worker_id(observation: Any, worker_id: str) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Return *observation* with ``worker_id`` set (frozen-safe).\"\"\"\n    if observation is None or not worker_id:\n        return observation\n    if getattr(observation, \"worker_id\", None) == worker_id:\n        return observation\n    try:\n        return dataclasses.replace(observation, worker_id=worker_id)\n    except (TypeError, ValueError):\n        try:\n            object.__setattr__(observation, \"worker_id\", worker_id)\n        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best effort\n            pass\n        return observation\n\n\ndef stamp_observations(observations: Iterable[Any], worker_id: str) -> tuple:\n    \"\"\"Stamp a batch of observations with the producing worker's id.\"\"\"\n    return tuple(stamp_worker_id(o, worker_id) for o in (observations or ()))\n\n\nasync def publish_worker_observations(observations: Iterable[Any], worker_id: str,\n                                      hub: Optional[Any] = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Publish a remote worker's observations to the observation hub.\"\"\"\n    stamped = list(stamp_observations(observations, worker_id))\n    if not stamped:\n        return 0\n    if hub is None:\n        try:\n            from core.observation.hub import get_hub\n            hub = get_hub()\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — hub is optional\n            logger.debug(\"observation hub unavailable: %s\", exc)\n            return 0\n    publisher = getattr(hub, \"publish\", None) or getattr(hub, \"publish_observation_async\", None)\n    if publisher is None:\n        return 0\n    for observation in stamped:\n        result = publisher(observation)\n        if hasattr(result, \"__await__\"):\n            await result\n    return len(stamped)\n\n\n__all__ = [\"stamp_worker_id\", \"stamp_observations\", \"publish_worker_observations\"]\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"LocalWorker — an in-process worker endpoint.\n\nExecutes through the canonical ``process_message`` (Rule 36) so a local\nworker and a remote worker behave identically.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport time\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\nfrom core.distribution.contracts import (\n    HealthStatus,\n    WorkerRequest,\n    WorkerResponse,\n)\n\n\nclass LocalWorker:\n    \"\"\"Runs requests against the local pipeline.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, worker_id: str = \"local\", pipeline: Any = None) -> None:\n        self.worker_id = worker_id\n        self.pipeline = pipeline\n        self.execution_count = 0\n\n    async def execute(self, request: WorkerRequest) -> WorkerResponse:\n        from core.pipeline.messages import Request\n        from core.pipeline.pipeline import process_message\n\n        self.execution_count += 1\n        started = time.monotonic()\n        body = request.request if isinstance(request, WorkerRequest) else request\n        if isinstance(body, Request):\n            msg = body\n        elif isinstance(body, dict):\n            msg = Request(text=str(body.get(\"text\") or \"\"),\n                          transport=str(body.get(\"transport\") or \"worker\"))\n        else:\n            msg = Request(text=str(body or \"\"), transport=\"worker\")\n        try:\n            response = await process_message(msg)\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — surface as a failed response\n            return WorkerResponse(\n                outcome=None, observations=(), metrics=None,\n                worker_id=self.worker_id, error=f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\",\n                success=False,\n                duration_ms=(time.monotonic() - started) * 1000,\n            )\n        return WorkerResponse(\n            outcome=response,\n            observations=(),\n            metrics=None,\n            worker_id=self.worker_id,\n            error=getattr(response, \"error\", None),\n            success=not getattr(response, \"error\", None),\n            duration_ms=(time.monotonic() - started) * 1000,\n        )\n\n    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:\n        return HealthStatus.HEALTHY\n\n    async def heartbeat(self) -> None:\n        return None\n\n    async def shutdown(self) -> None:\n        return None\n\n\n__all__ = [\"LocalWorker\"]\n"
}

WorkerResponse\nfrom core.distribution.pool import WorkerPool\nfrom core.distribution.registry import get_worker_registry\nfrom core.distribution.runtime import RemoteExecutionRuntime\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass DistributionScheduler:\n    \"\"\"Routes work to the best available worker, or runs it locally.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, runtime: Optional[RemoteExecutionRuntime] = None,\n                 pool: Optional[WorkerPool] = None,\n                 registry: Any = None) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry if registry is not None else get_worker_registry()\n        self.pool = pool or WorkerPool(self.registry.all_workers())\n        self.runtime = runtime or RemoteExecutionRuntime(registry=self.registry)\n\n    def refresh_pool(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Rebuild the pool from the current registry contents.\"\"\"\n        self.pool = WorkerPool(self.registry.all_workers())\n\n    async def dispatch(self, request: Any,\n                       affinity: Optional[ExecutionAffinity] = None) -> WorkerResponse:\n        affinity = affinity or ExecutionAffinity()\n        if affinity.worker_id is None:\n            selected = self.pool.next_worker(\n                tenant_id=affinity.tenant_id, capability=affinity.capability)\n            if selected is not None:\n                affinity.worker_id = selected.worker_id\n        return await self.runtime.execute(request, affinity=affinity)\n\n    async def dispatch_many(self, requests: Iterable[Any],\n                            affinity: Optional[ExecutionAffinity] = None) -> list:\n        out = []\n        for request in requests or ():\n            out.append(await self.dispatch(request, affinity=affinity))\n        return out\n\n\n__all__ = [\"DistributionScheduler\"]\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"Distributed graph domain model.\n\n``DistributedGraph`` is a dependency-aware DAG of :class:`GraphNode`s. All\ndependency resolution is local — no worker state is consulted (Rule 44) — and\nsnapshots are plain JSON-serialisable dicts (Rule 45).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Any, Iterable, Optional\n\n\nclass NodeStatus(str, Enum):\n    \"\"\"Lifecycle of a single graph node.\"\"\"\n\n    PENDING = \"pending\"\n    RUNNING = \"running\"\n    COMPLETED = \"completed\"\n    FAILED = \"failed\"\n    CANCELLED = \"cancelled\"\n\n    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic\n        return str(self.value)\n\n\nclass GraphState(str, Enum):\n    \"\"\"Lifecycle of a whole graph.\"\"\"\n\n    PENDING = \"pending\"\n    RUNNING = \"running\"\n    COMPLETED = \"completed\"\n    FAILED = \"failed\"\n    CANCELLED = \"cancelled\"\n\n    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic\n        return str(self.value)\n\n\nTERMINAL_NODE_STATUSES = Any:\n    if request is None:\n        return None\n    if isinstance(request, dict):\n        return dict(request)\n    payload = {}\n    for attr in (\"text\", \"transport\", \"user_id\", \"session_id\"):\n        if hasattr(request, attr):\n            payload[attr] = getattr(request, attr)\n    return payload or str(request)\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass GraphNode:\n    \"\"\"A single unit of work in the graph.\"\"\"\n\n    id: str\n    request: Any = None\n    status: NodeStatus = NodeStatus.PENDING\n    worker_id: Optional[str] = None\n    affinity_hint: Optional[str] = None\n    max_retries: int = 0\n    attempts: int = 0\n    result: Any = None\n    error: Optional[str] = None\n    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        self.id = str(self.id or \"\").strip()\n        if not self.id:\n            raise ValueError(\"GraphNode.id is required\")\n        if not isinstance(self.status, NodeStatus):\n            self.status = NodeStatus(str(self.status))\n\n    @property\n    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:\n        return self.status in TERMINAL_NODE_STATUSES\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"id\": self.id,\n            \"status\": self.status.value,\n            \"worker_id\": self.worker_id,\n            \"request\": _serialize_request(self.request),\n            \"attempts\": self.attempts,\n            \"error\": self.error,\n        }\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass GraphEdge:\n    \"\"\"A directed dependency: ``source`` must finish before ``target`` starts.\"\"\"\n\n    source: str\n    target: str\n\n    def __iter__(self):\n        yield self.source\n        yield self.target\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n        return {\"source\": self.source, \"target\": self.target}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass DistributedGraph:\n    \"\"\"A dependency-aware DAG of nodes.\"\"\"\n\n    id: str\n    nodes: dict = field(default_factory=dict)\n    edges: list = field(default_factory=list)\n    state: GraphState = GraphState.PENDING\n    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        self.nodes = {str(k): v for k, v in dict(self.nodes or {}).items()}\n        self.edges = [\n            e if isinstance(e, GraphEdge) else GraphEdge(str(e[0]), str(e[1]))\n            for e in (self.edges or [])\n        ]\n        if not isinstance(self.state, GraphState):\n            self.state = GraphState(str(self.state))\n\n    # ── mutation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    def add_node(self, node: GraphNode) -> GraphNode:\n        if not isinstance(node, GraphNode):\n            raise TypeError(\"add_node() expects a GraphNode\")\n        self.nodes[node.id] = node\n        return node\n\n    def get_node(self, node_id: str) -> Optional[GraphNode]:\n        return self.nodes.get(str(node_id))\n\n    def add_edge(self, edge: GraphEdge) -> GraphEdge:\n        if not isinstance(edge, GraphEdge):\n            edge = GraphEdge(str(edge[0]), str(edge[1]))\n        if edge not in self.edges:\n            self.edges.append(edge)\n        return edge\n\n    # ── dependency resolution (local only) ──────────────────────────\n    def get_dependencies(self, node_id: str) -> list:\n        \"\"\"Direct upstream nodes of *node_id*.\"\"\"\n        return to_snapshot(self) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"JSON-serialisable immutable snapshot of the graph (Rule 45).\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"graph_id\": self.id,\n            \"state\": from_snapshot(cls, snapshot: dict, original_nodes: Optional[dict] = None) -> \"DistributedGraph\":\n        \"\"\"Rebuild a graph from a snapshot plus the caller's node objects.\"\"\"\n Returns [(node, worker_id)].\"\"\"\n        assignments: list = []\n        ready = graph.get_ready_nodes()\n        if not ready:\n            return assignments\n        registry = self._registry()\n        for node in ready:\n            candidates = registry.discover(capability=node.metadata.get(\"capability\"))\n            eligible = [\n                reg for reg in candidates\n                if registry.check_version_compatibility(reg).compatible\n            ]\n            chosen = self._select(node, eligible)\n            if chosen is None:\n                continue\n            node.worker_id = chosen.worker_id\n            node.status = NodeStatus.RUNNING\n            assignments.append((node, chosen.worker_id))\n        if assignments and graph.state == GraphState.PENDING:\n            graph.state = GraphState.RUNNING\n        return assignments\n\n    async def on_node_failed(self, graph: DistributedGraph, node_id: str,\n                             reason: str = \"\") -> list:\n        \"\"\"Mark *node_id* FAILED and cancel every downstream node.\"\"\"\n        node = graph.get_node(node_id)\n        if node is not None:\n            node.status = NodeStatus.FAILED\n            node.error = reason or node.error\n        cancelled: list = []\n        for downstream in graph.get_downstream_nodes(node_id):\n            if downstream.status in (NodeStatus.COMPLETED, NodeStatus.FAILED):\n                continue\n            downstream.status = NodeStatus.CANCELLED\n            downstream.error = downstream.error or f\"upstream {node_id} failed\"\n            cancelled.append(downstream)\n        if cancelled:\n            logger.info(\"cancelled %d downstream node(s) after %s failed\",\n                        len(cancelled), node_id)\n        return cancelled\n\n    async def on_node_completed(self, graph: DistributedGraph, node_id: str,\n                                result: Any = None) -> None:\n   "content": "\"\"\"GraphCheckpointer — durable JSON snapshots of distributed graphs.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\nDEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_DIR = \"data/checkpoints\"\n\n\nclass GraphCheckpointer:\n    \"\"\"Writes/reads ``<graph_id>.json`` snapshots under a directory.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, directory: Any = None) -> None:\n        self.directory = Path(directory or DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_DIR)\n\n    def _path(self, graph_id: str) -> Path:\n        return self.directory / f\"{graph_id}.json\"\n\n    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:\n        self.directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    async def save(self, graph: Any) -> str:\n        \"\"\"Persist *graph*'s snapshot. Returns the written path.\"\"\"\n        self._ensure_dir()\n        snapshot = graph.to_snapshot() if hasattr(graph, \"to_snapshot\") else dict(graph)\n        path = self._path(snapshot.get(\"graph_id\", getattr(graph, \"id\", \"graph\")))\n        with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            json.dump(snapshot, handle, indent=2, default=str)\n        return str(path)\n\n    async def load(self, graph_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:\n        path = self._path(graph_id)\n        if not path.exists():\n            return None\n        try:\n            with open(path, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n                return json.load(handle)\n        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:\n            logger.warning(\"failed to load checkpoint %s: %s\", path, exc)\n            return None\n\n    async def list_checkpoints(self) -> list:\n        if not self.directory.exists():\n            return []\n        return sorted(p.stem for p in self.directory.glob(\"*.json\"))\n\n    async def delete(self, graph_id: str) -> bool:\n        path = self._path(graph_id)\n        if not path.exists():\n            return False\n        try:\n            os.remove(path)\n            return True\n        except OSError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - filesystem race\n            logger.warning(\"failed to delete checkpoint %s: %s\", path, exc)\n            return False\n\n\n__all__ = [\"GraphCheckpointer\", \"DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT_DIR\"]\n"
}

Completed graphs are not recovered.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\nfrom core.distribution.graph.checkpoint import GraphCheckpointer\nfrom core.distribution.graph.models import (\n    DistributedGraph,\n    GraphState,\n    NodeStatus,\n)\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass GraphRecovery:\n    \"\"\"Restores interrupted graphs to a re-runnable state.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, checkpointer: Optional[GraphCheckpointer] = None) -> None:\n        self.checkpointer = checkpointer or GraphCheckpointer()\n\n    async def recover(self, graph_id: str, original_nodes: Optional[dict] = None) -> Optional[DistributedGraph]:\n        \"\"\"Rebuild *graph_id* from its checkpoint, or None when not recoverable.\"\"\"\n        snapshot = await self.checkpointer.load(graph_id)\n        if not snapshot:\n            return None\n        state = str(snapshot.get(\"state\", GraphState.PENDING.value))\n        if state in (GraphState.COMPLETED.value, GraphState.CANCELLED.value):\n            logger.info(\"graph %s is %s — nothing to recover\", graph_id, state)\n            return None\n\n        graph = DistributedGraph.from_snapshot(snapshot, original_nodes or {})\n        # Everything non-terminal is re-armed for execution.\n        for node in graph.nodes.values():\n            if node.status in (NodeStatus.RUNNING, NodeStatus.FAILED):\n                node.status = NodeStatus.PENDING\n                node.error = None\n        graph.state = GraphState.PENDING\n        return graph\n\n\n__all__ = [\"GraphRecovery\"]\n"

ExecutionAffinity,\n    WorkerRequest,\n    WorkerResponse,\n)\nfrom core.distribution.graph.models import (\n    DistributedGraph,\n    GraphNode,\n    GraphState,\n    NodeStatus,\n)\nfrom Transport\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass GraphExecutor:\n    \"\"\"Executes graph nodes in dependency order.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, scheduler: Optional[DependencyAwareScheduler] = None,\n                 registry: Any = None,\n                 transport: Optional[Transport] = None) -> None:\n        self.registry = registry if registry is not None else get_worker_registry()\n        self.scheduler = scheduler or DependencyAwareScheduler(self.registry)\n        self.transport = transport\n        self._cancelled = False\n        self._inflight: dict = {}\n\n    # ── execution ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    async def execute(self, graph: DistributedGraph) -> DistributedGraph:\n        \"\"\"Run every node; returns the graph with its final state.\"\"\"\n        self._cancelled = False\n        self._inflight = {}\n        graph.state = GraphState.RUNNING\n        try:\n            while not           self._inflight = {}\n        finally:\n            self._inflight = {}\n\n        if self._cancelled:\n            for node in graph.nodes.values():\n                if not node.is_terminal:\n                    node.status = NodeStatus.CANCELLED\n            graph.state = GraphState.CANCELLED\n        elif graph.state == GraphState.RUNNING:\n            if transport = InProcessTransport(worker_fn=worker_fn)\n        return await transport.send(request)\n\n    # ── control ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    async def cancel(self,       """ReasonerStage — the single Reasoner abstraction (audit Rule 6).
      
      Complexity assessment + ReasoningResult construction.
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import re
      
      from core.pipeline.base import PipelineStage, StageOutcome, StageResult
      from core.pipeline.pipeline import PipelineContext
      from core.pipeline.reasoning_result import Belief, ReasoningResult
      
      _SIMPLE_MAX_CHARS = 120
      _MULTI_STEP_RE = re.compile(
          r"\b(research|compare|analyz|design|plan|implement|investigate|"
          r"evaluate|multi.?step)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
      
      
      class ReasonerStage(PipelineStage):
          @property
          def name(self) -> str:
              return "reasoning"
      
          def assess_complexity(self, text: str) -> str:
              if not text:
                  return "simple"
              if len(text) > _SIMPLE_MAX_CHARS or _MULTI_STEP_RE.search(text):
                  return "multi_step"
              return "simple"
      
          async def execute(self, context: PipelineContext) -> StageResult:
              text = str(getattr(context, "raw_input", "") or "")
              complexity = self.assess_complexity(text)
              services = getattr(context, "services", None)
              import uuid as _uuid
      
              rid_raw = services.uuid4() if services is not None and hasattr(services, "uuid4") \
                  else _uuid.uuid4().hex
              rid = f"rsn_{rid_raw[:24]}"
      
              confidence = 0.9 if complexity == "simple" else 0.7
              belief = Belief(belief_id=f"{rid[:16]}_b1",
                              claim=text[:120] or "empty request",
                              confidence=confidence, status="accepted")
              context.reasoning_result = ReasoningResult(
                  reasoning_id=rid,
                  activity_id=getattr(context, "activity_id", "") or "",
                  complexity=complexity,
                  beliefs=(belief,),
                  evidence=(),
                  contradictions=(),
                  counter_hypotheses=(),
                  confidence=confidence,
              )
              context.reasoning_assessment = {
                  "complexity": complexity, "confidence": confidence,
              }
              return StageResult(outcome=StageOutcome.CONTINUE, context=context)
      
      
      __all__ = ["ReasonerStage"]
      
  referencedBy: {}

      def _rbac_allows(tool_type: str, owner: Optional[str]) -> bool:
          """Consult the existing authz/policy engines; unknown tools are denied.
      
          The existing single-user security model (core.tools.security) governs the
          default: an admin/single-user owner passes the authz gate; a non-admin
          owner must be explicitly granted the tool scope.  This gate only ever
          narrows execution — it never widens permissions.
          """
          try:
              from core.authz import AuthContext
              from core.authz.engine import authz_engine
              from core.tools.security import owner_is_admin_or_single_user
              if owner_is_admin_or_single_user(owner):
                  context = AuthContext(
                      user_id=owner or "single_user",
                      scopes={"tools:execute:*"},
                  )
              else:
                  context = AuthContext(user_id=str(owner or "user"), scopes=set())
              return bool(authz_engine.evaluate(context, "tools:execute:" + tool_type))
          except Exception as exc:
              logger.debug("[execution] authz unavailable, denying %s: %s", tool_type, exc)
              return False

"""MemoryStage — decides what to persist from this request (Rule 2/3 owner).

Decisions:
  verification failed            -> IGNORE
  empty execution output         -> IGNORE
  otherwise                      -> STORE with a classified store_type:
    preference / project / fact / conversation (keyword classification).

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

from core.pipeline.base import PipelineStage, StageOutcome, StageResult
from core.pipeline.pipeline import PipelineContext
from core.pipeline.store_decision import StoreAction, StoreDecision


_PREFERENCE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(my favorite|i prefer|i like|i love|i hate|my preferred|"
    r"favorite|favourite)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
_PROJECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(i am working on|working on a|my project|the project|"
    r"new project|our project|repo|repository)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
_FACT_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(remember that|remember this|note that|keep in mind|"
    r"the fact that|fact:)\b", re.IGNORECASE)


class MemoryStage(PipelineStage):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        return "memory"

    def _classify(self, ctx: PipelineContext) -> str:
        raw = str(getattr(ctx, "raw_input", "") or "")
        if _PREFERENCE_RE.search(raw):
            return "preference"
        if _PROJECT_RE.search(raw):
            return "project"
        if _FACT_RE.search(raw):
            return "fact"
        return "conversation"

    async def execute(self, context: PipelineContext) -> StageResult:

"""Activity models — immutable-by-convention activity graph nodes/edges."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Optional


class ActivityStatus(str, Enum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    RUNNING = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    CANCELLED = "cancelled"


@dataclass
class ActivityNode:
    node_id: str
    activity_id: str = ""
    node_type: str = "goal"
    label: str = ""
    status: ActivityStatus = ActivityStatus.PENDING
    parent_id: Optional[str] = None
    resource_scope: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    created_at: Optional[datetime] = None
    updated_at: Optional[datetime] = None
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "node_id": self.node_id,
            "activity_id": self.activity_id,
            "node_type": self.node_type,
            "label": self.label,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "parent_id": self.parent_id,
            "resource_scope": dict(self.resource_scope),
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat() if self.created_at else None,
        }

"""ActivityManager — builds and maintains the activity graph."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Optional

from core.activity.models import ActivityEdge, ActivityNode, ActivityStatus


class ActivityManager:
    """In-memory activity graph with tenant-safe parent/child linking."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:

from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class DynamicMeta(type):
    def __getattr__(cls, name: str) -> Any:
        return name

@dataclass
class ActivityRecorder(metaclass=DynamicMeta):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        for k, v in kwargs.items():
            setattr(self, k, v)
    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any:
        return lambda *a, **kw: None
    def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> Any:
        return self
    async def __aenter__(self):

      """ActivityRecorder unit tests — planner-side activity recording."""
      
      import os
      import shutil
      import tempfile
      import unittest
      from unittest.mock import MagicMock, PropertyMock
      
      from core.activity.manager import ActivityManager
      from core.activity.models import ActivityStatus
      from core.activity.recorder import ActivityRecorder
      from core.activity.storage import ActivityStore
      from core.planner.models import SubGoal
      
      
      class TestActivityRecorder(unittest.TestCase):
          """Unit tests for ActivityRecorder."""
      
          def setUp(self):
              self._tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
              self._db = os.path.join(self._tmp, "test_recorder.db")
              self.store = ActivityStore(db_path=self._db)
              self.mgr = ActivityManager(store=self.store)
              self.recorder = ActivityRecorder(self.mgr)
      
          def tearDown(self):
              shutil.rmtree(self._tmp, ignore_errors=True)
      
          def _make_plan(self, *leaf_descriptions: str) -> SubGoal:
              """Build a SubGoal tree with one leaf per description."""
              root = SubGoal(id="root", description="root", template_id="research_build_email")
              for i, desc in enumerate(leaf_descriptions):
                  leaf = SubGoal(
                      id=f"leaf_{i}",
                      description=desc,
                      step_name="build" if "build" in desc.lower() else "research",
                  )
                  root.children.append(leaf)
              return root
      
          # ── Goal recording ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
          def test_01_record_goal(self):
              node = self.recorder.record_goal("Build coffee shop app",
                                                template_id="android_app_build")
              self.assertIsNotNone(node)
              self.assertEqual(node.node_type, "goal")
              self.assertEqual(node.depth, 0)
              self.assertEqual(self.recorder.activity_id, node.node_id)
              self.assertEqual(self.recorder.activity.node_id, node.node_id)
      
          def test_02_record_goal_no_template(self):
              node = self.recorder.record_goal("Simple task")
              self.assertIsNotNone(node)
              self.assertEqual(node.metadata, {})
      
          # ── Subgoal recording ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
          def test_03_record_subgoals(self):
              self.recorder.record_goal("Build app")
              plan = self._make_plan("Research competitors", "Build the APK",
                                      "Email results")
              self.recorder.record_subgoals(plan)
              tree = self.recorder.get_activity_tree()
              # root + 3 subgoals
              self.assertEqual(len(tree), 4)
              subgoal_nodes = [n for n in tree if n.node_type == "subgoal"]
              self.assertEqual(len(subgoal_nodes), 3)
      
          def test_04_record_subgoals_no_activity(self):
              # Without recording a goal first, no crash
              plan = self._make_plan("Research")
              self.recorder.record_subgoals(plan)
              # No activity yet, but no crash
              self.assertIsNone(self.recorder.activity_id)
      
          # ── Agent task recording ────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
          def test_05_record_agent_tasks(self):
              self.recorder.record_goal("Build app")
              tasks = [
                  {"agent_id": "research_agent", "goal": "Research competitors",
                   "step": "research", "parameters": {}},
                  {"agent_id": "build_agent", "goal": "Build APK",
                   "step": "build", "parameters": {"feature": "auth"}},
              ]
              self.recorder.record_agent_tasks(tasks)
              tree = self.recorder.get_activity_tree()
              agent_nodes = [n for n in tree if n.node_type == "agent_call"]
              self.assertEqual(len(agent_nodes), 2)
              self.assertEqual(agent_nodes[0].agent_id, "research_agent")
              self.assertEqual(agent_nodes[1].agent_id, "build_agent")
      
          def test_06_record_agent_tasks_no_activity(self):
              tasks = [{"agent_id": "a", "goal": "Task", "step": "build"}]
              self.recorder.record_agent_tasks(tasks)  # No crash
      
          # ── Task result recording ──────────────────────────────────────────────
      
          def test_07_record_task_success(self):
              self.recorder.record_goal("Build")
              task = {"agent_id": "builder", "goal": "Build APK", "step": "build"}
              self.recorder.record_agent_tasks([task])
              self.recorder.record_task_result(task, success=True,
                                                output={"artifacts": {"apk": "art_001"}})
              tree = self.recorder.get_activity_tree()
              agent_node = [n for n in tree if n.node_type == "agent_call"][0]
              self.assertEqual(agent_node.status, ActivityStatus.COMPLETED)
              self.assertEqual(agent_node.artifacts.get("apk"), "art_001")
      
          def test_08_record_task_failure(self):

              self.recorder.record_agent_tasks([task])
              self.recorder.record_task_result(task, success=False, error="Compile error")
              tree = self.recorder.get_activity_tree()
              agent_node = [n for n in tree if n.node_type == "agent_call"][0]
              self.assertEqual(agent_node.status, ActivityStatus.FAILED)
      
          def test_09_record_task_artifacts(self):

    def link_parent_child(self, parent_id: str, child_id: str) -> None:
        """Link two nodes, rejecting cross-tenant parent/child relations."""
        parent = self.nodes.get(parent_id)
        child = self.nodes.get(child_id)
        if parent is None or child is None:
            raise ValueError("parent and child must exist before linking")
        p_tenant = (parent.resource_scope or {}).get("tenant_id", "default")
        c_tenant = (child.resource_scope or {}).get("tenant_id", "default")
        if p_tenant != c_tenant:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cross-tenant parent/child link rejected: "
                f"parent tenant {p_tenant!r} != child tenant {c_tenant!r}")
        child.parent_id = parent_id
        self.edges.append(ActivityEdge(src=parent_id, dst=child_id))

    def set_status(self, node_id: str, status: ActivityStatus) -> bool:
        node = self.nodes.get(node_id)
        if node is None:
            return False
        node.status = status
        return True

    def children(self, parent_id: str) -> list[ActivityNode]:
        return [n for n in self.nodes.values() if n.parent_id == parent_id]

      """Tests for ResourceScope — canonical resource ownership marker.
      
      Sprint 4 covers the structural definition, pipeline propagation,
      and artifact threading.  Tenant-scoped storage backends are later.
      """
      
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      from datetime import datetime, timezone
      
      import pytest
      
      from core.identity import ResourceScope, Visibility
      from core.identity.resource_scope import DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
      
      _NOW = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
      from core.pipeline.context import PipelineContext
      from core.pipeline.messages import Request
      from core.pipeline.pipeline import Pipeline, get_pipeline, process_message, set_pipeline
      from core.pipeline.stages.auth import AuthenticationStage
      from core.pipeline.stages.authorization import AuthorizationStage
      
      # ── ResourceScope contract tests ──────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      
      class TestResourceScopeContract:
          """ResourceScope behaves like a frozen runtime artifact."""
      
          def test_frozen(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="tenant-1")
              with pytest.raises(Exception):
                  rs.tenant_id = "tenant-2"
      
          def test_defaults(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="tenant-1")
              assert rs.tenant_id == "tenant-1"
              assert rs.workspace_id is None
              assert rs.owner_id is None
              assert rs.visibility == Visibility.TENANT
              assert rs.metadata == {}
      
          def test_all_fields(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(
                  tenant_id="acme",
                  workspace_id="dev",
                  owner_id="user-42",
                  visibility=Visibility.PRIVATE,
              )
              assert rs.tenant_id == "acme"
              assert rs.workspace_id == "dev"
              assert rs.owner_id == "user-42"
              assert rs.visibility == Visibility.PRIVATE
      
          def test_equality(self):
              rs1 = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", workspace_id="w1")
              rs2 = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", workspace_id="w1")
              assert rs1 == rs2
      
          def test_hashable(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1")
              d = {rs: "value"}
              assert d[rs] == "value"
      
          def test_different_tenant_not_equal(self):
              rs1 = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1")
              rs2 = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t2")
              assert rs1 != rs2
      
      
      # ── Sentinel constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      
      class TestSentinelConstants:
          def test_default_tenant_id_is_migration_sentinel(self):
              assert DEFAULT_TENANT_ID == "__default__"
      
          def test_system_tenant_id_is_reserved(self):
              from core.identity.resource_scope import SYSTEM_TENANT_ID
              assert SYSTEM_TENANT_ID == "__system__"
      
      
      # ── Invariant validation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      
      class TestResourceScopeInvariants:
          def test_private_requires_owner(self):
              with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="PRIVATE visibility requires an owner_id"):
                  ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.PRIVATE)
      
          def test_private_with_owner_ok(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.PRIVATE, owner_id="alice")
              assert rs.owner_id == "alice"
      
          def test_workspace_visibility_requires_workspace_id(self):
              with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="WORKSPACE visibility requires a workspace_id"):
                  ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.WORKSPACE)
      
          def test_workspace_with_id_ok(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.WORKSPACE, workspace_id="w1")
              assert rs.workspace_id == "w1"
      
          def test_public_with_workspace_id_conflict(self):
              with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="PUBLIC visibility conflicts with a non-None workspace_id"):
                  ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.PUBLIC, workspace_id="w1")
      
          def test_public_without_workspace_ok(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.PUBLIC)
              assert rs.visibility == Visibility.PUBLIC
      
          def test_default_visibility_no_invariant_violation(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1")
              assert rs.visibility == Visibility.TENANT
              assert rs.owner_id is None  # TENANT doesn't require owner
      
      
      # ── Helper methods ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      
      class TestResourceScopeHelpers:
          def test_is_system_true(self):
              from core.identity.resource_scope import SYSTEM_TENANT_ID
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id=SYSTEM_TENANT_ID)
              assert rs.is_system() is True
              assert rs.is_default() is False
      
          def test_is_system_false(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="real-tenant")
              assert rs.is_system() is False
      
          def test_is_default_true(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id=DEFAULT_TENANT_ID)
              assert rs.is_default() is True
              assert rs.is_system() is False
      
          def test_is_default_false(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="real-tenant")
              assert rs.is_default() is False
      
          def test_real_tenant_neither(self):
              rs = ResourceScope(tenant_id="acme-corp")
              assert rs.is_system() is False
              assert rs.is_default() is False
      
      
      class TestResourceScopeSystemVisibility:
          def test_system_visibility_rejected_on_resource(self):
              with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="SYSTEM visibility is reserved"):
                  ResourceScope(tenant_id="t1", visibility=Visibility.SYSTEM)
      
      
      # ── Visibility enum ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      
      class TestVisibilityEnum:
          def test_values(self):
              assert Visibility.PRIVATE.value == "private"
              assert Visibility.TENANT.value == "tenant"
              assert Visibility.WORKSPACE.value == "workspace"
              assert Visibility.PUBLIC.value == "public"
      
          def test_order(self):
              values = list(Visibility)
              assert values == [Visibility.PRIVATE, Visibility.TENANT, Visibility.WORKSPACE, Visibility.PUBLIC, Visibility.SYSTEM]
      
      
      # ── Pipeline context propagation ──────────────────────────────────────────────
      
      
      @pytest.mark.asyncio
      class TestResourceScopePipeline:
          """ResourceScope is populated in process_message()."""
      
          async def test_resource_scope_present_after_process_message(self):
              """process_message populates resource_scope with tenant info."""
              old = get_pipeline()
              try:
                  p = Pipeline()
                  p.add_stage(AuthenticationStage())
                  p.add_stage(AuthorizationStage())
                  set_pipeline(p)
      
                  req = Request(text="hello", transport="test", user_id="user-1")
                  resp = await process_message(req)
                  assert resp is not None
                  # Re-run with a capture to inspect context
              finally:
                  set_pipeline(old)
      
          async def test_resource_scope_has_default_tenant(self):
              """No tenant info → defaults to 'default' tenant."""
              from core.pipeline.base import PipelineStage, StageOutcome, StageResult
      
              captured = None
      
              class CaptureStage(PipelineStage):
                  @property
                  def name(self) -> str:
                      return "capture"
      
                  async def execute(self, context: PipelineContext) -> StageResult:
                      nonlocal captured
                      captured = context.resource_scope
                      return StageResult(outcome=StageOutcome.CONTINUE, context=context)
      
              old = get_pipeline()
              try:
                  p = Pipeline()
                  p.add_stage(AuthenticationStage())
                  p.add_stage(CaptureStage())
                  set_pipeline(p)
      
                  req = Request(text="hello", transport="test")
                  resp = await process_message(req)
                  assert captured is not None
                  assert captured.tenant_id == DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
                  assert captured.visibility == Visibility.TENANT
              finally:
                  set_pipeline(old)

              finally:

          async def test_resource_scope_ownership_readonly(self):
              """resource_scope is owned by load_context — no other stage writes it."""
              from core.pipeline.base import PipelineStage, StageOutcome, StageResult
      
              class MutatorStage(PipelineStage):

"""Outcome — terminal runtime artifact of one Activity (Sprint 5.5C contract)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, List, Optional

from core.pipeline.observation import Observation


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Outcome:
    """Immutable summary of one activity execution (Rule 30 scope carrier)."""

    activity_id: str
    success: bool = False
    observations: List[Observation] = field(default_factory=list)
    status: str = ""
    error: Optional[str] = None
    resource_scope: Any = None
    metrics: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "activity_id": self.activity_id,
            "success": self.success,
            "status": self.status,
            "error": self.error,
            "resource_scope": (
                self.resource_scope.to_dict()
                if hasattr(self.resource_scope, "to_dict")
                else self.resource_scope
            ),
            "observations": [o.to_dict() for o in self.observations],
            "metrics": dict(self.metrics),
        }


__all__ = ["Outcome"]

  "path": "core/identity/resource_scope.py",
  "instructions": "Implement the full ResourceScope contract: sentinels, visibility ordering, invariants, helpers.",
  "content": "\"\"\"Resource and visibility scope models.\n\n``ResourceScope`` is the frozen ownership marker carried on every runtime\nartifact (observations, outcomes, metrics). Invariants are enforced at\nconstruction time so an invalid scope can never enter the graph.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, field\nfrom enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Any, Optional\n\n\nclass Visibility(str, Enum):\n    \"\"\"Who may see a resource.\n\n    Ordering is significant (narrowest → widest, plus the reserved system\n    tier); tests assert the declaration order.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    PRIVATE = \"private\"\n    TENANT = \"tenant\"\n    WORKSPACE = \"workspace\"\n    PUBLIC = \"public\"\n    SYSTEM = \"system\"\n\n\n#: Migration sentinel for rows/artifacts that predate tenancy.\nDEFAULT_TENANT_ID = \"__default__\"\n\n#: Reserved tenant for system-owned artifacts.\nSYSTEM_TENANT_ID = \"__system__\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ResourceScope:\n    \"\"\"Logical partition key: resources/events belong to a tenant+scope.\"\"\"\n\n    tenant_id: str = DEFAULT_TENANT_ID\n    user_id: Optional[str] = None\n    owner_id: Optional[str] = None\n    workspace_id: Optional[str] = None\n    visibility: Visibility = Visibility.TENANT\n    metadata: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict, compare=False)\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.visibility is Visibility.SYSTEM:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"SYSTEM visibility is reserved and cannot be set on a resource\")\n        if self.visibility is Visibility.PRIVATE and not self.owner_id:\n            raise ValueError(\"PRIVATE visibility requires an owner_id\")\n        if self.visibility is Visibility.WORKSPACE and not self.workspace_id:\n            raise ValueError(\"WORKSPACE visibility requires a workspace_id\")\n        if self.visibility is Visibility.PUBLIC and self.workspace_id is not None:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"PUBLIC visibility conflicts with a non-None workspace_id\")\n\n    # ── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    def is_system(self) -> bool:\n        return self.tenant_id == SYSTEM_TENANT_ID\n\n    def is_default(self) -> bool:\n        return self.tenant_id == DEFAULT_TENANT_ID\n\n    def matches(self, other: \"ResourceScope\") -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Same-tenant match (public scopes match across tenants).\"\"\"\n        if self.visibility == Visibility.PUBLIC or \\\n                other.visibility == Visibility.PUBLIC:\n            return True\n        return self.tenant_id == other.tenant_id\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        return {\n            \"tenant_id\": self.tenant_id,\n            \"user_id\": self.user_id,\n            \"owner_id\": self.owner_id,\n            \"workspace_id\": self.workspace_id,\n            \"visibility\": self.visibility.value,\n        }\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic\n        return (f\"ResourceScope(tenant_id={self.tenant_id!r}, \"\n                f\"visibility={self.visibility.value!r})\")\n\n\ndef default_scope(**kwargs: Any) -> ResourceScope:\n    \"\"\"Build a default (tenant-scoped) resource scope.\n\n    Construction belongs to this definition module and to the pipeline's\n    ``process_message()``; other modules should ask for a scope here rather\n    than instantiating one themselves (architecture Rule 19).\n    \"\"\"\n    return ResourceScope(**kwargs)\n\n\n__all__ = [\"ResourceScope\", \"Visibility\", \"DEFAULT_TENANT_ID\",\n           \"SYSTEM_TENANT_ID\", \"default_scope\"]\n"
}

# Plan: turn JARVIS into a real automation system

**Ground rule:** the test suite is the spec. I don't invent abstractions — every module I revive must be demanded by a test or an existing caller. The architecture audit (~60 rules) is the design doc and stays as a required gate.

- Canonical path exists: `core/pipeline` 26 stages, `jarvis_provider.py` (Ollama/cloud), permission + capability gates, specialists (browser/desktop/coding/research), distribution layer with worker registry/graph.
- But: **~400 files are still `DynamicStub` placeholders**, 60 architecture tests fail (identity/resource contracts), ~36 unit modules can't even import, and nothing has been run live against Ollama. An automation system can't be built on that; it has to be de-poisoned first, in priority order.

## Phases (each ends in a gate, not a promise)

**0. Stub inventory & triage** — script that lists every `DynamicStub` file with: does a test cover it? is it on the automation critical path? is it reachable from `process_message`? Output = ordered worklist. Gate: live dashboard of stub count, goes to 0 on the critical path.

**1. Backbone contracts** — fix the 60 identity/resource failures (`resource_access`, `security_context`, `resource_grant`, `identity_models`, `pipeline_executor`, `deterministic`). This is the tenant/resource-scope spine: every automation artifact must carry `resource_scope` or tenant isolation breaks the moment you run two jobs. Gate: those 7 files green + audit green.

**2. Import surface to zero** — the ~36 unit modules that fail to import (missing names like `core.errors.NotFoundError`, whole modules like the `invalidation` package, `ControlInfo`, `stream_pipeline`). Gate: `pytest tests/` collects with **zero errors** — no automation work can be trusted until this holds.

**3. One execution path** — prove the loop end to end with no LLM: request → auth → tenant → plan → capability selection → permission → execution → verification → memory → reflection. Then live: Ollama up, real models, every stage emitting observations. Gate: replay/trace validation passes with a real model in the loop, and verification is evidence-based (never "the model said it worked").

**4. Specialists as loop tools** — browser, desktop, coding, research registered in the capability registry with permission profiles, so the *planner* can compose them instead of a human calling them. Each gets: real precondition check → execute → verify → retry → rollback, plus a health signal. Gate: the acceptance suites for each specialist pass against a real target (a real repo, a real page, a real window).

**5. Durability & scale** — scheduler queue backed by the store, crash recovery via graph checkpoints (`DistributionScheduler`/`GraphRecovery` are now real), worker version negotiation, idempotency keys, retry budgets. Gate: kill the process mid-run and the job resumes or fails cleanly — never half-done silently.

**6. Ops hardening** — quarantine after repeated permission violations, circuit breakers on failing providers, cost/latency metrics per capability, secret handling, structured logs. Gate: a failure matrix test (provider down, worker gone, permission denied, model timeout) that all degrade to a typed error, not a hang.

**7. Make it stay fixed** — CI that runs the tiers: fast unit/contract on every change, architecture audit as required, live Ollama smoke nightly. Gate: a PR that reintroduces a stub or an alternate path fails automatically.

Phase 1–2 first (they're the actual blockers and I've already got momentum + the tooling in my head). Phases 3–4 are where "it automates things" becomes demonstrable. 5–7 are what makes it trustworthy overnight.

import this module dynamically.\"\"\"\n    module = rel[:-3].replace(\"/\", \".\")\n    leaf = module.rsplit(\".\", 1)[-1]\n    patterns = (\n        f'import_module(\"{module}\")', f\"import_module('{module}')\",\n        f'import_module(\"{leaf}\")', f\"import_module('{leaf}')\",\n        f'__import__(\"{module}\")', f\"__import__('{module}')\",\n str]] = []\n    for path in sorted(ROOT.rglob(\"*.py\")):\n        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts):\n            continue\n        rel = _rel(path)\n        if rel.startswith((\"tests/\", \"scripts/\")) or path.name.startswith(\"test_\"):\n            continue\n        mod = module_name(rel)\n        try:\n            importlib.import_module(mod)\n        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — report everything\n            failures.append((mod, f\"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}\"))\n    return failures\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    parser = action=\"store_true\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n\n    if args.smoke:\n        failures = smoke_import()\n        for mod, err in failures:\n            print(f\"IMPORT-FAIL {mod}: {err}\")\n        print(f\"import failures: {len(failures)}\")\n        return 0\n\n    report = load_inventory()\n    recoverable = [r for r in report if r[\"recoverable_from_git\"]]\n    orphans = [r for r in report if r[\"priority\"] == \"P1\"]\n\n    sources = {}\n    for path in ROOT.rglob(\"*.py\"):\n        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts):\n            continue\n        sources[_rel(path)] = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n\n    deletable, guarded = [], []\n    for entry in orphans:\n        rel = entry[\"file\"]\n        if rel.endswith(\"__init__.py\"):\n            guarded.append((rel, \"package __init__\"))\n            continue\n        ext = external_references(rel)\n        dyn = dynamic_reference(rel, sources)\n {
  "path": "scripts/stub_cleanup.py",
  "replacements": [
    {
      "oldString": "def dynamic_reference(rel: str, sources: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:",
      "newString": "def python_references(rel: str, sources: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Non-stub Python files that import this module, including relative imports.\"\"\"\n    module = rel[:-3].replace(\"/\", \".\")\n    parts = module.split(\".\")\n    leaf = parts[-1]\n    package = \".\".join(parts[:-1])\n    patterns = [\n        f\"import {module}\", f\"from {module} import\",\n        f\"from {package} import {leaf}\",  # absolute sibling import\n        f\"from .{leaf} import\", f\"from . import {leaf}\",  # same package\n    ]\n    out = []\n    for other, text in sources.items():\n        if other == rel or \"DynamicStub\" in text:\n            continue\n        if any(p in text for p in patterns):\n            out.append(other)\n    return sorted(set(out))\n\n\ndef dynamic_reference(rel: str, sources: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:",
      "allowMultiple": false
    },
    {
      "oldString": "        ext = external_references(rel, corpus)\n        dyn = dynamic_reference(rel, sources)\n        if ext or dyn:\n            guarded.append((rel, f\"external={ext[:3]} dynamic={dyn[:3]}\"))",
      "newString": "        ext = external_references(rel, corpus)\n        dyn = dynamic_reference(rel, sources)\n        py = python_references(rel, sources)\n        if ext or dyn or py:\n            guarded.append((rel, f\"py={py[:3]} external={ext[:2]} dynamic={dyn[:2]}\"))",
      "allowMultiple": false
    }
  ]
}

      """De-poison the working tree: restore recoverable stubs, delete orphan ones.
      
      Safety model
      ------------
      1. "Recoverable" stubs get the real implementation restored from git history.
      2. "Orphan" stubs (no inbound reference from a non-stub module, no test mention)
         are deleted — but only after these guards pass:
           * the module path / leaf name does not appear in any non-Python file
             (yaml/json/toml/ini/md/sh/pyproject config, docs, scripts)
           * no dynamic import pattern (``importlib.import_module("x")`` /
             ``__import__("x")``) names the module
           * the file is not a package ``__init__.py``
      3. After deletion a whole-tree import smoke test runs; any module that fails to
         import because of a deletion is reported (and the deletion is a candidate for
         rollback).
      
      Everything is committed in git, so any deletion is revertible with
      ``git checkout <rev> -- <path>``.
      
      Usage:
          python scripts/stub_cleanup.py --dry-run     # guard report only
          python scripts/stub_cleanup.py --apply       # restore + delete
          python scripts/stub_cleanup.py --smoke       # import every module
      """
      from __future__ import annotations
      
      import argparse
      import importlib
      import json
      import re
      import subprocess
      import sys
      from pathlib import Path
      
      ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
      INVENTORY = ROOT / "stub_inventory.json"
      SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "__pycache__", "node_modules", ".venv", "venv", "dist", "build"}
      # Runtime/config surfaces only — docs (.md) and generated reports do not
      # reference code at runtime, so mentioning a module there must not block a
      # deletion. This inventory file is excluded explicitly (it lists every stub).
      NON_PY_TEXT_SUFFIXES = {
          ".yaml", ".yml", ".json", ".toml", ".ini", ".cfg", ".sh",
          ".ps1", ".html", ".ts", ".js",
      }
      CORPUS_EXCLUDE = {"stub_inventory.json", "stub_cleanup.json"}
      
      
      def _rel(path: Path) -> str:
          return path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
      
      
      def _git(*args: str) -> str:
          result = subprocess.run(
              ["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
              encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
          )
          return result.stdout or ""
      
      
      def load_inventory() -> list[dict]:
          if not INVENTORY.exists():
              sys.exit("run scripts/stub_inventory.py first")
          return json.loads(INVENTORY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
      
      
      MAX_CORPUS_BYTES = 400_000
      
      
      def text_corpus() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
          """Read every non-Python text file once: [(relpath, text), ...]."""
          corpus: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
          for path in ROOT.rglob("*"):
              if not path.is_file() or any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts):
                  continue
              if path.name in CORPUS_EXCLUDE:
                  continue
              if path.suffix.lower() not in NON_PY_TEXT_SUFFIXES and path.name not in (
                  "Makefile", "Dockerfile", "requirements.txt"
              ):
                  continue
              try:
                  if path.stat().st_size > MAX_CORPUS_BYTES:
                      continue
                  corpus.append((_rel(path), path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")))
              except OSError:
                  continue
          return corpus
      
      
      def external_references(rel: str, corpus: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[str]:
          """Non-Python files that name this module (path or leaf word)."""
          module = rel[:-3].replace("/", ".")
          leaf = module.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
          path_hit = re.compile(re.escape(module))
          leaf_hit = re.compile(rf"\b{re.escape(leaf)}\b")
          hits: list[str] = []
          for other, text in corpus:
              if path_hit.search(text) or leaf_hit.search(text):
                  hits.append(other)
          return sorted(set(hits))
      
      
      def python_references(rel: str, sources: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
          """Non-stub Python files that import this module, including relative imports."""
          module = rel[:-3].replace("/", ".")
          parts = module.split(".")
          leaf = parts[-1]
          package = ".".join(parts[:-1])
          patterns = [
              f"import {module}", f"from {module} import",
              f"from {package} import {leaf}",  # absolute sibling import
              f"from .{leaf} import", f"from . import {leaf}",  # same package
          ]
          out = []
          for other, text in sources.items():
              if other == rel or "DynamicStub" in text:
                  continue
              if any(p in text for p in patterns):
                  out.append(other)
          return sorted(set(out))
      
      
      def dynamic_reference(rel: str, sources: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:
          """Python files that import this module dynamically."""
          module = rel[:-3].replace("/", ".")
          leaf = module.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
          patterns = (
              f'import_module("{module}")', f"import_module('{module}')",
              f'import_module("{leaf}")', f"import_module('{leaf}')",
              f'__import__("{module}")', f"__import__('{module}')",
              f'__import__("{leaf}")', f"__import__('{leaf}')",
          )
          out = []
          for other, text in sources.items():
              if other == rel:
                  continue
              if any(p in text for p in patterns):
                  out.append(other)
          return out
      
      
      def module_name(rel: str) -> str:
          mod = rel[:-3].replace("/", ".")
          return mod[: -len(".__init__")] if mod.endswith(".__init__") else mod
      
      
      def smoke_import() -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
          """Import every importable module; return (module, error) failures."""
          failures: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
          for path in sorted(ROOT.rglob("*.py")):
              if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts):
                  continue
              rel = _rel(path)
              if rel.startswith(("tests/", "scripts/")) or path.name.startswith("test_"):
                  continue
              mod = module_name(rel)
              try:
                  importlib.import_module(mod)
              except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — report everything
                  failures.append((mod, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"))
          return failures
      
      
      def main() -> int:
          parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
          parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
          parser.add_argument("--apply", action="store_true")
          parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
          args = parser.parse_args()
      
          if args.smoke:
              failures = smoke_import()
              for mod, err in failures:
                  print(f"IMPORT-FAIL {mod}: {err}")
              print(f"import failures: {len(failures)}")
              return 0
      
          report = load_inventory()
          recoverable = [r for r in report if r["recoverable_from_git"]]
          orphans = [r for r in report if r["priority"] == "P1"]
      
          sources = {}
          for path in ROOT.rglob("*.py"):
              if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in path.parts):
                  continue
              sources[_rel(path)] = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
      
          corpus = text_corpus()
          print(f"external text corpus: {len(corpus)} files")
          deletable, guarded = [], []
          for entry in orphans:
              rel = entry["file"]
              if rel.endswith("__init__.py"):
                  guarded.append((rel, "package __init__"))
                  continue
              ext = external_references(rel, corpus)
              dyn = dynamic_reference(rel, sources)
              py = python_references(rel, sources)
              if ext or dyn or py:
                  guarded.append((rel, f"py={py[:3]} external={ext[:2]} dynamic={dyn[:2]}"))
              else:
                  deletable.append(rel)
      
          print(f"recoverable:      {len(recoverable)}")
          print(f"orphan candidates:{len(orphans)}")
          print(f"safe to delete:   {len(deletable)}")
          print(f"kept (guarded):   {len(guarded)}")
          for rel, why in guarded[:15]:
              print(f"  guarded {rel}: {why}")
      
          if args.dry_run or not args.apply:
              print("\n(dry run — pass --apply to act)")
              return 0
      
          for entry in recoverable:
              rel, rev = entry["file"], entry["recoverable_from_git"]
              print(f"restoring {rel} <- {rev[:10]}")
              _git("checkout", rev, "--", rel)
      
          if deletable:
              # Only tracked paths: an untracked pathspec aborts the whole `git rm`.
              tracked = set(_git("ls-files", "--", *deletable).split("\n"))
              tracked.discard("")
              to_remove = [rel for rel in deletable if rel in tracked]
              untracked = [rel for rel in deletable if rel not in tracked]
              if to_remove:
                  result = subprocess.run(
                      ["git", "rm", "-q", "--ignore-unmatch", "--", *to_remove],
                      cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                  )
                  if result.returncode != 0:
                      print(f"git rm failed: {result.stderr.strip()[:300]}")
              for rel in untracked:
                  target = ROOT / rel
                  if target.exists():
                      target.unlink()
              print(f"deleted {len(to_remove)} tracked + {len(untracked)} untracked "
                    f"orphan stub modules")
      
          print("\nnow run: python scripts/stub_cleanup.py --smoke")
          return 0
      
      
      if __name__ == "__main__":
          sys.exit(main())
      
  referencedBy: {}

> Careful: matching leaf-only `import foo` would over-match common leaves (e.g., `models`, `utils`). Over-matching is safe (keeps more files). The risk of over-matching is keeping poison — acceptable; under-matching deletes needed modules — unacceptable. So bias toward keeping.
> 
> Simplify: a file references `rel` if any import line's target == module, or target == f"{package}.{leaf}" (same thing), or target starts with module + ".", or the import line is `from {package} import {leaf}` (covered by target==package with imported names) — need to check the imported names for that case.
> 
> Let me implement: parse each import line into (level, module, names). Then:
> - `from X import Y`: referenced if X == module, or X == package and Y == leaf, or X.startswith(module+"."), or (X in ("",".") and Y==leaf) for relative same-package, or X is a relative name resolving to package and Y == leaf.
> - `import X`: referenced if X == module, or X == package and ... no. Also `import a.b.c` binds 'a' but loads the submodule → referenced if module == X or module.startswith(X+".")? If someone does `import core.tools`, then `core.tools.schemas` isn't loaded. But `import core.tools.schemas` loads it. So referenced if X == module or X.startswith(module+".")

> Relative imports: `from . import schemas` inside package core.tools → level=1, module="" → package = current file's dir. Need the file's package. I have `other` rel path → dirname. So compute base = dirname(other).replace('/','.') then walk up (level-1).

1\n    base = parts[: len(parts) - up] if up else parts\n    return \".\".join([*base, mod]) if mod else \".\".join(base)\n\n\ndef python_references(rel: str, sources: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Python files that import this module, including relative imports.\n\n    Stub files are NOT skipped: the auto-reconstructed stubs keep the original\n    module's ``# Re-exports`` block, so their import lines are real references.\n    Ignoring them previously deleted modules that load-bearing ``__init__.py``\n    stubs still import (e.g. ``core.tools.schemas``).\n    \"\"\"\n    module = rel[:-3].replace(\"/\", \".\")\n    parts = module.split(\".\")\n    leaf = parts[-1]\n    package = \".\".join(parts[:-1])\n    out = []\n    for other, text in sources.items():\n        if other == rel:\n            continue\n        hit = False\n        for m in _IMPORT_LINE.finditer(text):\n            if m.group(\"plain\"):\n                target = m.group(\"plain\")\n                if target == module or target.startswith(module + \".\"):\n                    hit = True\n                    break\n                continue\n            target = _resolve(m.group(\"level\"), m.group(\"mod\"), other)\n            names = [n.strip().split(\" as \")[0].strip()\n                     for n in m.group(\"names\").split(\",\") if n.strip()]\n            if target == module or target.startswith(module + \".\"):\n                hit = True\n                break\n            if target == package and leaf in names:\n                hit = True\n                break\n        if hit:\n            out.append(other)\n    return sorted(set(out))",
